//2: adapted for doomalay v0.42). Phase 1 root-cause investigation (read errors,
//3: reproduce, check recent changes, evidence at every component boundary) ->
//4: Phase 2 pattern analysis (working examples, differences) -> Phase 3 single
//5: hypothesis + minimal test -> Phase 4 failing-test fix. NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT
//6: CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST. Pass the bug report / error / failing test as the
task: <FILL ME IN: bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior>

stages.name: phase1_root_cause
stages.instructions: PHASE 1 - ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION, before ANY fix is proposed. Bulleted findings with evidence citations only. Work through: (1) Read the error messages COMPLETELY - stack traces, line numbers, error codes; the exact solution is often in them. (2) Reproduce consistently - exact steps, does it happen every time; if not reproducible, gather more data, do not guess. (3) Check recent changes - git diff, recent commits, new dependencies, config changes. (4) Multi-component systems: gather evidence at EVERY component boundary BEFORE proposing anything - for each boundary, what data enters, what exits, which environment/config propagates, state at each layer; run once to show WHERE it breaks, then investigate the failing component. (5) Trace data flow backward - where does the bad value originate, what called this with it; keep tracing up to the source (fix at source, not symptom). Every finding cites file:line or the exact command + output. If you catch yourself writing a fix here, STOP - that is Phase 4.

stages.name: phase2_pattern
stages.instructions: PHASE 2 - PATTERN ANALYSIS. Output JSON {"working_examples": [{"where": str, "what_works": str}], "differences": [str], "dependencies": [str]}. Find similar WORKING code in the same codebase; if implementing a pattern, read the reference COMPLETELY (don't skim - every line). List EVERY difference between working and broken, however small - never assume 'that can't matter'. List what the failing path depends on: other components, settings, config, environment, assumptions.

stages.name: phase3_hypothesis
stages.instructions: PHASE 3 - HYPOTHESIS. Output JSON {"hypothesis": str, "evidence": str, "minimal_test": str, "predicted_result": str}. Form ONE hypothesis stated clearly: 'I think <X> is the root cause because <Y>' - specific, not vague; write it down. The minimal test is the SMALLEST possible change to test it - one variable at a time; if you need to change multiple things at once, you have multiple hypotheses. predicted_result says what observing it proves or refutes. If you don't know, say 'I don't understand <X>' - never pretend.

stages.name: phase4_fix
stages.instructions: PHASE 4 - IMPLEMENTATION. Fix the ROOT CAUSE, not the symptom: (1) create the simplest failing test case reproducing the bug (it must fail before the fix, pass after - use the TDD flow); (2) implement the SINGLE fix addressing the identified root cause - no 'while I'm here' improvements, no bundled refactoring, one change at a time; (3) verify: the covering test passes, no other tests broke, the original symptom is actually resolved. IF THE FIX DOES NOT WORK: STOP - count your attempts; after fewer than 3, return to Phase 1 with the new information; at 3 or more failed fixes, the pattern indicates an ARCHITECTURAL problem (each fix reveals new coupling elsewhere / requires massive refactoring / creates new symptoms) - say so explicitly and question the fundamentals instead of attempting fix #4.

stages.name: verify
stages.instructions: Output JSON {"pass": bool, "reason": str}. pass=false if ANY of: a fix was proposed before root-cause evidence (Phase 1 skipped or thin); more than one variable changed in the hypothesis test; the fix has no failing-test-first reproduction; the fix addresses a symptom rather than the traced source; 'while I'm here' changes bundled in; 3+ fix attempts continued without an architecture question. Otherwise pass=true.

llm_judges: Does the fix address the traced root cause at its source rather than a downstream symptom?
Was exactly one variable changed per hypothesis test, with the hypothesis stated before testing?
